summary: EARTHPULSE is an AI-powered environmental intelligence platform that combines satellite data, geospatial analytics, and artificial intelligence to monitor and visualize changes across Earth's surface. It aims to transform complex satellite observations into meaningful, actionable environmental insights. The platform focuses on major areas: wildfire and forest loss, glacier tracking, and climate anomaly detection. By integrating environmental datasets from multiple sources, EARTHPULSE addresses challenges such as fragmented data, complex historical analysis, and time-consuming manual interpretation. Its current prototype primarily focuses on glacier intelligence using historical WGMS datasets and thermal anomaly detection using NASA FIRMS data. It also incorporates interactive geographical visualization and AI-assisted scientific interpretation to identify environmental trends, understand changes, and support informed decision-making. In future will be putting and implementing rainforest and earthquake also
details: EARTHPULSE is an AI-powered Earth observation and environmental intelligence platform designed to monitor global glacier retreat, analyze satellite imagery, and detect fire and thermal anomalies. It integrates historical glacier data from the World Glacier Monitoring Service (WGMS), covering over 214,600 glaciers, with NASA FIRMS MODIS datasets spanning 210 countries. Using technologies such as FastAPI, LangGraph, Google Gemini, GeoPandas, and Rasterio, the platform features an autonomous AI agent that retrieves scientific data, performs numerical analysis, validates results, and generates detailed reports. Its key capabilities include glacier mass balance monitoring, glacier retreat analysis, fire hotspot detection, Fire Radiative Power (FRP) analysis, SAR and optical satellite data processing, and geospatial change detection. Additionally, EARTHPULSE provides real-time REST APIs and GeoJSON outputs for integration with the AtlasX interactive 3D globe, transforming complex satellite observations into meaningful scientific insights for environmental monitoring and climate research.
